topic: Marks of a wise mind amid calamity
text: They that do not strive for objects that are unattainable, that do not grieve for what is lost and gone, that do not suffer their minds to be clouded amid calamities, are regarded to possess intellects endued with wisdom.

topic: Prudence toward friend and foe
text: He is a wise person who doth not disregard even a weak foe; who proceeds with intelligence in respect of a foe, anxiously watching for an opportunity; who doth not desire hostilities with persons stronger than himself; and who displayeth his prowess in season.

topic: Keeping counsel concealed until acted upon
text: He whose intended acts, and proposed counsels remain concealed from foes, and whose acts become known only after they have been done, is considered wise.

topic: How calamity reveals true friends
text: A brave man is tested during a season of panic; he that is self-controlled, in times of poverty; and friends and foes, in times of calamity and danger.

topic: Mastering anger and joy to win prosperity
text: He that restraineth the force of both anger and joy, and never, O king, loseth his senses under calamities, winneth prosperity.

topic: Forgiveness as the quiet strength of the strong
text: Endued with forgiveness, they betray no outward symptoms of wrath and are quiet like fire in wood.

topic: The three expedients of policy: conciliation, gift, and disunion
text: The acquisition of dominion should be made by the three well-known means (of conciliation, gift, and disunion).

topic: Acting against a foe only once you command sufficient strength
text: If one be weak one should pay court to one's foe that is stronger, even if the latter deserves death; but one should kill that foe as soon as one commandeth sufficient strength, for, if not killed, dangers soon arise from him.

topic: Helping helpless relatives brings enduring prosperity
text: He that helpeth his poor and wretched and helpless relatives, obtain children and animals and enjoyeth prosperity that knoweth no end.

topic: No amount of earthly wealth can satiate one person's greed
text: Thy paddy, wheat, gold, animals, and women that are on earth all cannot satiate even one person.

topic: Heavenly wealth over earthly wealth makes one unconquerable
text: They that are poor in earthly but rich in heavenly wealth and sacrifices, become unconquerable and fearless, and they should be regarded as embodiments of Brahman.

topic: Standing alone invites destruction, even for the mighty
text: The tree that stands singly, though gigantic and strong and deep-rooted, hath its trunk soon smashed and twisted by a mighty wind.

topic: What is the greatest wonder?
text: Yaksha: What is most wonderful? Yudhishthira: Day after day countless creatures are going to the abode of Yama, yet those that remain behind believe themselves to be immortal. What can be more wonderful than this?

topic: What is true happiness?
text: Yaksha: Who is truly happy? Yudhishthira: a man who cooketh in his own house, on the fifth or the sixth part of the day, with scanty vegetables, but who is not in debt and who stirreth not from home, is truly happy.

topic: Who is truly learned?
text: Yaksha: What man should be regarded as learned? Yudhishthira: He is to be called learned who knoweth his duties.

topic: What is the path?
text: Yaksha: What is the path? Yudhishthira: Argument leads to no certain conclusion, the Srutis are different from one another; there is not even one Rishi whose opinion can be accepted by all; the truth about religion and duty is hid in caves: therefore, that alone is the path along which the great have trod.

topic: Who is the true enemy?
text: Yaksha: What enemy is invincible? Yudhishthira: Anger is an invincible enemy.

topic: What is grief?
text: Yaksha: What, O king, is ignorance? And what is pride? What also is to be understood by idleness? And what hath been spoken of as grief? Yudhishthira: True ignorance consists in not knowing one's duties. Pride is a consciousness of one's being himself an actor or sufferer in life. Idleness consists in not discharging one's duties, and ignorance in grief.

topic: Protection of subjects is a king's foremost duty
text: Protection of the subject, O Yudhishthira, is the very chief of kingly duties. The divine Vrihaspati does not applaud any other duty so much as this one. All of them praise the duty of protection, O foremost of virtuous persons, in respect of kings.

topic: Qualities to look for when choosing a counsellor
text: That person who is possessed of intelligence and memory, who is clever in the transaction of business, who is naturally averse from cruelty, who never indulges in wrath, and who, whether regarded or disregarded is never dissatisfied, be he thy priest or preceptor or honoured friend, should always receive thy worship if he accepts the office of thy counsellor and resides in thy abode.

topic: Taxation should be gentle, like a bee gathering honey
text: A king should milk his kingdom like a bee gathering honey from plants, without injuring the plant from which it is gathered. The king should, in the matter of taxes, act like the leech, which drinks blood mildly, without the knowledge of the person from whom it draws it.

topic: Without the king's rod of punishment, the strong devour the weak
text: If there were no king on earth for wielding the rod of chastisement, the strong would then have preyed on the weak after the manner of fishes in the water. It hath been heard by us that men, in days of old, in consequence of anarchy, met with destruction, devouring one another like stronger fishes devouring the weaker ones in the water.

topic: Choosing when to make peace and when to wage war with rivals
text: Make peace with those foes with whom, according to the ordinance, peace should be made, and wage war with them with whom war should be waged.

topic: A ruler's own conduct becomes an example others imitate
text: A person governed by passion indulges in stimulants and meat, and appropriates the wives and the wealth of other people, and sets a bad example for imitation by others.

topic: Patience lets a king achieve his goals even with limited means
text: A king possessed of patience and without any fault may, if he likes, obtain the fruition of all his wishes, with the aid of even a small force.

topic: In dire circumstances, preserve life first and pursue higher duty afterward
text: One should, when one is dying, preserve one's life by any means in one's power without judging of their character. Afterwards, when competent, one should seek the acquisition of merit.

topic: A kingdom's wellbeing directly reflects the king's integrity
text: The peace and prosperity of subjects are all dependent on the king. If the king happens to be good, prosperity is seen among the people; if the king becomes oppressive and sinful, prosperity disappears, and every kind of evil sets in.

episode: Bhagavad Gītā — Kṛṣṇa's counsel to Arjuna
topic: Duty without attachment to the fruits of action
text: Thy concern is with work only, but not with the fruit (of work). Let not the fruit be thy motive for work; nor let thy inclination be for inaction.

episode: Bhagavad Gītā — Kṛṣṇa's counsel to Arjuna
topic: Rejecting despondency and rising to act
text: Whence, O Arjuna, hath come upon thee, at such a crisis, this despondency that is unbecoming a person of noble birth? Let no effeminacy be thine, O son of Kunti. This suits thee not. Shaking off this vile weakness of heart, arise, O chastiser of foes.

episode: Bhagavad Gītā — Kṛṣṇa's counsel to Arjuna
topic: Self-mastery — the self as friend or enemy
text: One should raise his self by self; one should not degrade his self; for one's own self is one's friend, and one's own self is one's enemy. To him only who has subjugated his self by his self is self a friend. But to him who has not subjugated his self, his self behaves inimically like an enemy.

episode: Bhagavad Gītā — Kṛṣṇa's counsel to Arjuna
topic: Steadiness of the wise
text: When one casts off all the desires of his heart and is pleased within his self with self, then is one said to be of steady mind. He whose mind is not agitated amid calamities, whose craving for pleasure is gone, who is freed from attachment to worldly objects, fear and wrath, is said to be a Muni of steady mind.

episode: Bhagavad Gītā — Kṛṣṇa's counsel to Arjuna
topic: Action over inaction
text: No one can abide even for a moment without doing work. All works are, in every way, done by the qualities of nature. He, whose mind is deluded by egoism, however, regards himself as the actor.

episode: Bhagavad Gītā — Kṛṣṇa's counsel to Arjuna
topic: Leading by example — the responsibility of the capable
text: Whatever a great man doth, is also done by vulgar people. Ordinary men follow the ideal set by them, the great.

episode: Bhagavad Gītā — Kṛṣṇa's counsel to Arjuna
topic: Transcending fear through the teaching of the eternal soul
text: Know that the soul to be immortal by which all this universe is pervaded. No one can compass the destruction of that which is imperishable. It is never born, nor doth it ever die. Weapons cleave it not, fire consumeth it not; the waters do not drench it, nor doth the wind waste it. Therefore, knowing it to be such, it behoveth thee not to mourn for it.

topic: Choosing loyalty to a benefactor over a righteous cause
text: Karna said to Krishna: For the sake of death, or the ties of blood, or fear, or temptation, I cannot venture, O Janardana, to behave falsely towards the intelligent son of Dhritarashtra. I cannot venture to destroy those bonds even for the sake of the whole earth or heaps of gold.

episode: Ashvatthama's act — the ethics of revenge
topic: Revenge that violates the codes of war
text: Ashvatthama's night attack on the sleeping Pandava camp was condemned even by its victims: he never slaughters one that is asleep, or one that is heedless, or one that has laid aside his weapons — yet this is precisely what was done. Dhrishtadyumna and all the sons of Draupadi were slain while they slept.

topic: Choosing diplomacy before war
text: Krishna said: Let a person, virtuous and honest and of respectable birth, and wary — an able ambassador — set out to beseech them mildly for inducing them to give half the kingdom to Yudhishthira.

topic: Building a coalition of allies swiftly
text: Drupada said: Let speedy messengers go to Salya, and Dhrishtaketu, and Jayatsena, and the prince of the Kekayas. Rightminded persons respond to the request of those that first beseech them. Therefore, make haste in first preferring your suit to these rulers of men.

topic: Blocked by one, the many fail to reach their own
text: Sanjaya narrated: the Matsyas, the Panchalas, the Kaikeyas, and the Pandavas, exerting themselves vigorously, succeeded in approaching the presence of Jayadratha — but none of them could bear him. Protected by a boon, he alone checked all of them and sealed the breach, leaving Abhimanyu cut off within the formation.

topic: Peace is the choice of the powerful, not weakness
text: Krishna said to Dhritarashtra: The establishment of peace, O king, depends on thee and myself, O monarch. In battle, O great king, nothing but wholesale destruction is visible. Reconciliation with the Pandavas, whom thou hast raised as thy own, is wisdom, not weakness.

topic: The strength of unity against a common threat
text: Krishna said to Dhritarashtra: If, O slayer of foes, thou hast both the Kurus and the Pandavas at thy back, the sovereignty of the whole world and invincibility before all foes will be thine.

topic: War brings only mutual destruction, whatever pride tells you
text: Krishna said: In battle, O great king, nothing but wholesale destruction is visible.

topic: Birth of Yudhishthira, son of the god Dharma
text: Then the handsome Kunti was united (in intercourse) with the god of justice in his spiritual form and obtained from him a son devoted to the good of all creatures. This first child of Pandu shall be known by the name of Yudhishthira.

topic: Birth of Bhima, son of the god Vayu
text: The god of wind thereupon begat upon her the child afterwards known as Bhima of mighty arms and fierce prowess.

topic: Birth of Arjuna, son of Indra
text: The celebrated Kunti, thus addressed by her lord, invoked Sakra (the king of the gods) who thereupon came unto her and begat him that was afterwards called Arjuna.

topic: Birth of Nakula and Sahadeva, sons of Madri via the Ashvins
text: Madri thought of the twin Aswins, who coming unto her with speed begat upon her two sons. In energy and beauty these twins shall transcend even the twin Aswins themselves.

topic: Birth of Karna, son of Kunti and the sun god Surya, before her marriage to Pandu
text: Thus speaking unto the daughter of Kuntibhoja, the illustrious Tapana — the illuminator of the universe — gratified his wish. And of this connection there was immediately born a son known all over the world as Karna accoutred with natural armour and with face brightened by ear-rings.

topic: Birth of Duryodhana and the hundred Kaurava sons to Gandhari
text: That ball of flesh then, sprinkled over with water, became, in time, divided into a hundred and one parts, each about the size of the thumb. Then in time, king Duryodhana was born from among those pieces of the ball of flesh that had been deposited in those pots. According to the order of birth, king Yudhishthira was the oldest.
